newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg to buy Lender's bagels business from Kraft.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg to buy Lender's bagels business from Kraft.

text.p: Kellogg Co. said Monday it will acquire the Lender's Bagels business from Kraft Foods Inc. for $455 million.
Lender's, based in White Plains, N.Y., is a large manufacturer and marketer of frozen, refrigerated and fresh bagels with annual sales of $275 million.
Kraft Foods is a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc.
The deal, expected to close by year-end, includes Lender's plants in West Haven/New Haven, Conn.; Mattoon, Ill.; and Buffalo, N.Y., Kellogg said.
"Lender's Bagels is a perfect fit for Kellogg Company's fast-growing convenience foods business," said Arnold G. Langbo, Kellogg's chairman and chief executive.

"With our heritage based in nutrition and our technical competence in grain-based food products, adding the nation's number one brand in bagels to our number one positions in toaster pastries, frozen waffles, and cereal bars offers substantial new opportunities to grow our business."
Kraft, based in Northfield, Ill., is the nation's largest packaged food company with revenues of $16 billion.
Kellogg, based in Battle Creek, Mich., is the world's largest producer of ready-to-eat cereal and a leader in grain-based convenience foods with revenues of $7 billion.
Kellogg's stock closed Friday at $68.25, while Philip Morris closed at $101.375, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
